statement: For a closed connected orientable surface of genus at least two, the centralizer of any transitive subgroup of Homeo(X) is finite. Every based loop in an arbitrary action centralizer whose values generate a transitive subgroup therefore contracts in that centralizer by the finite-action theorem. There exists an explicit closed torsion-free Polish subgroup G of Homeo(D2,boundary) with fundamental group Z; extending it by the identity embeds it closedly in every hyperbolic identity homeomorphism group, where the displayed generator is null-homotopic. The subgroup is not claimed to be a centralizer.

notes: The proof gives the exact evaluation identification C(K) -> N_K(K_x)/K_x inside X, proves inverse continuity, and projects the resulting compact free-action group injectively to the discrete mapping-class group. The supporting L1(Z)/Z example includes all quotient metrics, the Cantor/Banach embedding and the horizontal-shear embedding. It is not claimed to be a centralizer, and the general admissible infinite level-0 obligation remains unresolved.
